Hi Sam — thanks for the heads-up, and congrats on the launch. We can definitely support a plan like this. High level approach:

1) Baseline sizing: pick a committed slab that covers your normal 95th percentile daily traffic (we can run a profile off your recent 7-day telemetry).
2) Burst policy: attach an ephemeral burst pool with pre-warmed GPUs that can be routed in under 90s. We recommend a 40% headroom guardband for model warm cache variance during cold starts.
3) Autoscaling: continuous batching + instant scale steps for ephemeral pool; fallback to a compatible quantized variant if capacity saturated.
4) Costs/lead time: reserved slab (monthly) + burst hours billed at a premium; pre-warm requires 72h notice for guaranteed capacity.

I9m looping in Ben (pricing) and Marcus (runtime sizing) to draft a quick capacity proposal and a short SOW. Expect a draft by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Priya Natarajan

Priya / Marcus —

Quick pricing note for the strawman:
- Committed slab: pick N GPUs to cover baseline QPS. For OrbitAI telemetry (from Jordan) baseline translates to ~12 A100-equivalents for steady-state.
- Burst pool: recommend reserving a 24-GPU ephemeral pool with 2-stage pre-warm. Billing model we9ve used for similar deals: reserved slab price + burst reservation fee (one-time for pre-warm) + per-hour burst consumption at 1.8x standard rate.
- Minimum pre-warm window for guaranteed capacity: 72 hours (we can provision faster on best-effort if inventory allows).

I9ll add this into the SOW pricing tab. Marcus — can you confirm the 24 GPU burst sizing fits with our runtime headroom assumptions (model, sequence lengths, KV cache warm-up)?

Ben

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-21T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: OrbitAI burst sizing strawman

Ben — based on Jordan9s sample telemetry (session lengths, prefix reuse) a 24-GPU burst pool is a reasonable starting point. Notes:

- Model: 13B transformer with 2k typical context; KV cache warm-up for new prefixes adds ~15% extra token cost for first 2 minutes of traffic.
- Guardband: recommend 40-50% headroom if they rely on cold cache traffic profile during the spike. If they can pre-warm prefixes (recommended), headroom can drop to 20-25% and we can reduce burst pool to 16 GPUs.
- Autoscale steps: prefer 4x step policy (16 -> 32 -> 48 -> 64) timed to cumulative queue depth rather than linear CPU/GPU load to avoid jitter.
- Fallback: route to a quantized 8-bit variant preserving output fidelity within their eval thresholds if we hit 90% cluster utilization.

I9ll fold these details into the capacity_plan workbook for the SOW. Evelyn, can you confirm the SLA wording for p95 latency during burst and the telemetry hooks we9ll need?

Marcus
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: OrbitAI burst sizing strawman

Marcus / team —

SLA & observability items:
- SLA: we can commit to p95 < 400ms for the baseline committed slab. For burst windows we can guarantee p95 < 600ms if they accept the explicit fallback to the quantized variant for overflow routing. If they want hard p95 < 400ms during any overload we must increase guaranteed burst capacity accordingly (costs scale).
- Telemetry: need request_id, model_version, route_id, and prefix-cache-hit boolean for each request across the spike; sample traces at 1% for A/B quality checks.
- Alerts: a burst-activation alert with 5m rolling window and a runbook link; a capacity-exhaust alert at 85% utilization which triggers on-call paging to infra.

I9ll add a short SLA clause for the SOW and include the list of telemetry hooks in the drive doc.

Subject: OrbitAI dedicated burst plan (strawman) + next steps

Hi Sam / Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attaching a short strawman SOW and a capacity workbook (orbitai_capacity_plan_v1.xlsx) that contains three recommended configurations:

A) Conservative (baseline slab + 24 GPU burst, 40% headroom): higher cost, guaranteed p95 < 400ms with pre-warm
B) Optimized (baseline + 16 GPU burst, 25% headroom with prefix pre-warm): lower cost, p95 target 400ms with quantized fallback up to 600ms
C) Minimal (baseline only, no guaranteed burst; best-effort short-term burst at spot inventory): lowest cost, higher risk during spike

Key asks from OrbitAI to finalize:
- Confirm expected peak QPS and whether you can provide a list of hot prefixes we can pre-warm (this materially impacts headroom).
- Decision on hard SLA during burst vs. acceptance of quantized fallback path.
- Preferred billing model for burst (reserve-fee + per-hour consumption vs. all-hours committed).

If you9re good, we can convert the selected option into a formal SOW and a 72h pre-warm schedule. I9ve included a HubSpot link to the deal and the Drive folder with the draft SOW.
